reason: Examined published L2 completeness and density, the distributional Fourier automorphism and its L2 agreement proof, and the precise bilinear test pairing. A Cauchy class has a representative-independent weighted L2 limit; density makes the map onto. Cauchy-Schwarz against bracket-weighted Schwartz tests defines a tempered distribution, and testing a zero regular L2 functional against Schwartz approximants to conjugate(g) proves injection. The strategy checks weak and strong continuity and identifies initial Schwartz functions. Countable Choice is used only for the published completion, Fourier and density interfaces and selection of one approximation sequence.
